findings.description: The same list object stored in the cache is returned on both the miss path (`return hits`) and the hit path (`return entry[1]`). Before this change each call returned a fresh list. A caller that sorts, appends to or filters the result in place now silently corrupts the cached entry, and later callers with the same query get the altered results.
findings.suggestion: Store a tuple in the cache and return `list(...)` copies, or return a copy on both paths.
findings.title: Cached result list returned by reference; callers can mutate the cache

findings.description: An expired entry is popped, so the cache shrinks, and then a recompute happens. The capacity check on line 65 therefore sees a length that already excludes that key, which is fine. However, the stored entry keeps its original timestamp when re-inserted on a hit, so the TTL is absolute from creation and the LRU ordering has no effect on expiry. This is only a minor inconsistency, not a hard failure.
findings.suggestion: Document the TTL semantics, or drop the LRU reordering if it is not needed.
findings.title: Cache hit refreshes LRU order but not the timestamp, and expired entries are handled inconsistently
